newsitem.title: USA: Apache Qarun wells have potential pay.
newsitem.headline: Apache Qarun wells have potential pay.

text.p: Two exploratory wells Apache Corp is drilling on its Qarun Concession in Egypt's Western Desert have logged some 700 feet of indicated net pay zone, the company said Thursday.
The company said both wells are still drilling and the company expects to complete them and release test results in the next six weeks.
Apache, the operator, owns a 75 percent contractor interest in the Qarun Concession. Global Natural Resources Inc, which is soon to merge with Seagull Energy Corp, holds the remaining 25 percent.
The concession is operated by Qarun Petroleum Co, an Egyptian corporation owned jointly by the contractors and the Egyptian General Petroleum Corp, the national oil company.
Apache pointed out a well it drilled at Qarun two years ago, with 305 feet of net pay, tested at 11,957 barrels of oil per day -- one of the largest finds in Egypt's Western Desert.
That discovery prompted a visit from Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and a stepped up drilling program on the 1.9-million-acre concession.
Apache said one of the latest Qarun wells is still drilling toward its objective Jurassic formation, which has proved productive at a number of sites in the Western Desert.
